scope: Official-source survey packet for FBI CDE/UCR/BJS surfaces relevant to V2, focused on methodology differences, operational lane rules, and reconciliation guardrails.

naming_doctrine.finding: Starting with the 2024 public release, the FBI's annual umbrella release is 'Reported Crimes in the Nation' (RCN), and CIUS is one component inside it.

official_evidence.title: UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2024
official_evidence.detail: RCN 2024 lists CIUS, NIBRS, Hate Crime Statistics, and LEOKA as its components and says CIUS combines reported, estimated, and trended data.

official_evidence.title: Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2024 Frequently Asked Questions
official_evidence.detail: FAQ states that RCN 2024 includes CIUS 2024, NIBRS 2024, Hate Crime Statistics 2024, LEOKA 2024, and the UCR summary.

naming_doctrine.v2_rule: When V2 says 'CIUS annual bundle' for 2024+, interpret it as the CIUS component inside the broader RCN release, not as the whole release.

core_distinctions.finding: Publication tables and CDE/master/open-data surfaces are official but methodologically different lanes.

official_evidence.title: CDE Methodologies Explain Potential Differences in UCR Data
official_evidence.detail: Publication releases must pass internal quality reviews and may exclude data; CDE/master-style releases keep all reported data in file.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Never treat a mismatch between a publication table and an explorer/master/open-data surface as an automatic error; classify the methodology lane first.

core_distinctions.finding: CIUS tables 1-7 and CIUS tables 8-11 are not the same methodology lane.

official_evidence.title: Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2024 Frequently Asked Questions
official_evidence.detail: Traditional estimates in CIUS tables 1-7 approximate agencies without a complete 12 months of data.

official_evidence.title: CDE Find Info on CDE landing page
official_evidence.detail: The 2024 reported violent/property tables 8-11 are from agencies submitting 12 months of complete offense data.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Use tables 1-7 for official FBI estimate controls and tables 8-11 for published reported-agency counts; do not merge them into one city/state series.

core_distinctions.finding: Crime Explorer is a dynamic surface that mixes SRS and summarized NIBRS for violent/property views and uses NIBRS-only logic elsewhere.

official_evidence.title: CDE Crime Explorer Methodology
official_evidence.detail: Explorer methodology says violent/property offense pages consist of SRS data and summarized NIBRS data, while all other offenses include only NIBRS information.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Use Crime Explorer for monitoring and context, not as the annual canonical input lane for V2.

core_distinctions.finding: The Data Discovery Tool is a query surface that applies hierarchy-rule logic for violent/property selections.

official_evidence.title: CDE Data Discovery Tool
official_evidence.detail: DDT says violent/property counts reflect the hierarchy rule and are query-based rather than raw incident extraction.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Use DDT for agency lookup and query-based explanation, not as a raw-NIBRS substitute.

core_distinctions.finding: Participation data measure reporting coverage across any format and are not an agency roster or offense dataset.

official_evidence.title: CDE Participation download panel
official_evidence.detail: The participation panel says agencies are counted regardless of format and the purpose is to clarify population covered by reported data.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Use participation only for coverage denominators and transition context.

core_distinctions.finding: The public roster endpoint is current-status metadata, so year-specific regime audits must use nibrs_start_date.

official_evidence.title: CDE public agency roster endpoint
official_evidence.detail: Roster payload exposes is_nibrs and nibrs_start_date.

official_evidence.title: Packet-local roster_effective_year_guardrails.csv
official_evidence.detail: The anchored 2024 roster pull contains 481 agencies with is_nibrs=true but nibrs_start_date after 2024-12-31.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Derive effective_nibrs_2024 using nibrs_start_date <= 2024-12-31 before choosing a 2024 reporting-regime lane.

core_distinctions.finding: The FBI traditional SRS-derived estimate family and the BJS/FBI NIBRS-estimate family are complementary but distinct.

official_evidence.title: CDE SRS estimated crimes panel
official_evidence.detail: CDE says the SRS dataset reflects the estimates traditionally included in FBI annual publications.

official_evidence.title: Crime Known to Law Enforcement, 2024
official_evidence.detail: CKLE says NIBRS estimates use imputation and weighting and are based on the NIBRS Estimation Program.

official_evidence.title: UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2024
official_evidence.detail: The summary says traditional CIUS estimates are SRS plus NIBRS converted to SRS, while NIBRS-only estimates should be viewed as analogous measures.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Do not stitch these estimate families into one undifferentiated series without an explicit bridge note.

core_distinctions.finding: BJS current API endpoints publish revised prior-year estimates, while archive endpoints preserve originally published values.

official_evidence.title: BJS NIBRS National Estimates API
official_evidence.detail: The API page explains that late-transmitted incidents update prior years and provides archive endpoints for original values.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Pick current or archive endpoints intentionally depending on whether V2 wants latest best estimates or point-in-time reproducibility.

core_distinctions.finding: LEARCAT is an official BJS exploratory tool, but it is neither definition-identical to CDE nor universally covered.

official_evidence.title: LEARCAT Methodology
official_evidence.detail: LEARCAT notes different offense definitions for some categories and limits rates to full-reporter states with 90%+ coverage.

core_distinctions.v2_rule: Use LEARCAT as a secondary exploratory aid, not as the authority for matching CDE or CIUS counts.

fbi_publication_estimates_trend.decision_rule: Use CIUS tables 1-7 and CIUS trend resources when V2 needs official FBI annual estimates or same-agency trends.
mandatory_guardrails: CIUS estimate and trend outputs are not raw counts.
Do not compare CIUS estimates directly to raw NIBRS counts or participation counts without a bridge rule.

fbi_publication_agency_tables.decision_rule: Use CIUS tables 8-11 for published agency-level reported counts in 2024+ annual releases.
mandatory_guardrails: Only agencies with 12 months of complete offense data appear in these tables.
Use DDT or the roster only to explain exclusions or naming, not to backfill the publication table.

agency_roster_validation.decision_rule: Use the roster endpoint for ORI/name/type/current status fields and DDT for spot checks or interactive lookup.
mandatory_guardrails: Derive effective-year NIBRS status from nibrs_start_date.
Do not treat current is_nibrs as retrospective truth for 2024.

participation_coverage_context.decision_rule: Use participation data only for state-year agency and population coverage context.
mandatory_guardrails: Participation counts include summary and incident-based reporters.
Coverage context is not an offense input lane.

raw_nibrs_incident_detail.decision_rule: Use state NIBRS downloads for raw offense/victim/property detail and ORI-level incident support.
mandatory_guardrails: Expect differences from CIUS and DDT because they answer different counting questions.
Use raw NIBRS only where NIBRS coverage exists and is appropriate for the year.

historical_raw_master_continuity.decision_rule: Use annual master files when continuity of raw in-file data matters more than publication comparability.
mandatory_guardrails: Master files require extraction code and collection-specific handling.
This lane retains all reported data in file and is not publication-quality filtered.

historical_publication_continuity.decision_rule: Bridge historical FBI publications through 2019 to CIUS annual bundles in CDE/RCN for 2020+ publication-style continuity.
mandatory_guardrails: Keep the whole series in the publication lane.
Do not substitute master/open-data values to fill publication gaps without explicit disclosure.

bjs_national_estimates.decision_rule: Use the BJS API for machine pulls and CKLE for the human-readable benchmark publication.
mandatory_guardrails: This is an estimate lane, not a raw reported-count lane.
Choose current vs archive endpoints deliberately.

fbi_hosted_nibrs_estimation_tables.decision_rule: Use FBI-hosted NIBRS estimation tables only when V2 wants static download-table surfaces from CDE.
mandatory_guardrails: Treat this as the NIBRS-estimate family, not as CIUS continuity.
Prefer the BJS API when point-in-time reproducibility or machine access matters more than packaging.

methodology_guardrails.decision_rule: Read the methodology docs before reconciling two official counts from different FBI/BJS surfaces.
mandatory_guardrails: Classify each source as publication, estimate, raw/open-data, participation, agency metadata, or dynamic explorer before comparing values.
Treat methodology differences as the default explanation until the two surfaces are proven to be in the same lane.

current_monitoring.decision_rule: Use the dynamic CDE surfaces for current monitoring, not for annual canonical inputs.
mandatory_guardrails: Capture timestamps externally if outputs must be frozen.
Expect periodic pauses around annual release processing.

reconciliation_playbook: Start by labeling each source as publication_table, estimate_series, master_raw, participation_coverage, agency_metadata, or dynamic_explorer.
If two sources land in different methodology families, explain the family mismatch before investigating data defects.
Never compare CIUS tables 1-7 to CIUS tables 8-11 as if they answer the same question.
Never compare participation or roster metadata directly to offense totals; use them only to explain coverage or agency-regime differences.
When reconciling BJS estimates to FBI annual releases, decide whether the target is traditional CIUS estimates or NIBRS-only estimates; they are different lanes.
When reconciling a dynamic CDE value to an annual bundle, verify the explorer timestamp and whether annual publication processing paused or changed the dynamic surface.

do_not_compare_directly.reason: Tables 1-7 are traditional estimates/trends; tables 8-11 are reported-agency tables requiring 12 months of complete offense data.
Publication tables are quality-filtered; explorer/master/open-data surfaces retain all reported data in file or dynamic query outputs.
These are different estimate families with different underlying methodology and coverage assumptions.
Participation is state-year coverage context across any format; roster is agency metadata with current reporting-status fields.
DDT applies hierarchy-rule logic for violent/property counts; raw NIBRS does not collapse incidents the same way.
LEARCAT uses different offense-category definitions for some measures and only supports rates in full-reporter states.

promotable_doctrine.statement: Publication tables, raw/open-data files, dynamic explorers, participation datasets, and estimate products are separate lanes. V2 must choose one lane per metric and reconciliation task.
Inside CIUS, tables 1-7 are estimate/trend tables while tables 8-11 are reported-agency tables with a 12-month completeness filter.
Use Crime Explorer and DDT for monitoring and triage, not as canonical annual controls.
Treat public roster is_nibrs as current-status metadata and derive year-effective reporting status from nibrs_start_date.
Use participation data only for coverage context and denominators, never for offense totals or ORI roster authority.
Keep the traditional FBI SRS-derived estimate series separate from BJS/FBI NIBRS-only estimate series unless an explicit bridge is documented.
For BJS NIBRS estimates, current API endpoints give the latest revised values and archive endpoints preserve originally published values.

secondary_sources_used.purpose: Archival taxonomy only; retained because it can clarify legacy UCR component names if a V2 historical note needs it.
